passage: In the reception classroom, Mridul was fitting the last piece into his farm puzzle when Sumit shouted and snatched it from his hand, catching his wrist. Mridul's stomach dropped and he felt very small. His fist curled to hit back, but he stopped. "Stop, that hurts," he said, his voice wobbling. He stepped away and walked quickly to the teacher's desk. "Sumit grabbed me." The teacher came over and crouched between the two boys.

qa.q: What did Sumit snatch from Mridul's hand?
qa.a: He snatched the last piece of the farm puzzle.

qa.q: How was Mridul feeling when Sumit shouted and grabbed him?
qa.a: He felt scared and small, and his wobbly voice and dropped stomach show it. He also felt an urge to hit back.

qa.q: Why was stepping away and fetching the teacher a good choice?
qa.a: Hitting back would probably have made the fight bigger. Saying "stop, that hurts" and getting a trusted adult let the problem be sorted out fairly.

qa.q: How might Sumit have been feeling when he grabbed the piece?
qa.a: He probably wanted the piece badly and could not wait, and may have been angry or upset. He was probably surprised when Mridul stayed calm and went to get help.

grounding: A friend shouts or grabs and I feel scared and small; a wise child says stop, steps back and fetches a teacher.
